# The End of Vibe Coding! Introducing Specification-Driven Development (SDD)

The short video features specification-guided development (SDD) as a response to live coding problems. Explains the idea of specification as house plan, the four steps of the GitHub Spec Kit, the gains and the cost of keeping the specifications up to date.

Video by Maurício Yokoyama Issei, published on December 3, 2025 (1 min 57 s).
Watch: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nQfTaS__IVA

_The video and the transcript are in Portuguese. The minutes between brackets, such as [04:12], point to the excerpt of the video._

## The problem of vibe coding

According to the video, the live coding promised agility, but the lack of consistency frustrated many people: the result impresses the screen, but the code has bugs, is inconsistent and has no architecture [00:00].

The video cites that a quarter of the Y Combinator startups already had almost all the code generated by AI. The proposed exit is a more structured and formal approach [00:20].

## What is SDD

In the specification-guided development (SDD), the specification is the house plan, and the code is only the construction [00:20].

If the AI fails, the problem is not in the code, but in the specification, and that is where it is corrected [00:41].

## How it works

The video uses the GitHub Spec Kit as an example, with four steps [00:41]:

1. Specify: the focus is the user, what and why [01:01].
2. Plan: the technical plan for the AI agent [01:01].
3. Breaking into tasks: AI divides everything into small tasks [01:01].
4. Implement: AI executes, and those who develop check the result [01:01].

SDD does not replace TDD or BDD: it acts on a layer above, defining the intention of the product [01:01].

## Gains and costs

Teams get more aligned, and AI generates more consistent code. But the method requires discipline to write good specifications and keep them up to date [01:24].

The video leaves a question: SDD can exchange agility for a bureaucracy that only seems to provide security [01:24].

The role of those who develop changes: from writing code to designing systems and defining intention. The future may be less about coding and more about specifying clearly [01:45].

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Does SDD replace TDD?

Nope. According to the video, the SDD acts in a layer above, defining the intention of the product [01:01].

### Where is an AI error corrected in SDD?

In the specification. The code is construction; the specification is the plant [00:41].

## About the video

The Vibe Coding (development guided only by intuition and feeling) is on the count of days! The promise of code agility generated by unstructured AI resulted in bugs, inconsistency and weak architecture, leading large companies to rethink their strategies.

In this video, we present the Specification-Driven Development (SDD), the new formal and structured approach that is emerging as a response to the chaos of Vibe Coding.

What you'll learn:

The Vibe Coding Problem [00:05]: Because the lack of consistency and architecture in AI-generated codes, guided by loose prompts, has become a problem for startups.

What is SDD? [00:28]: Understand how SDD changes the focus from code to specification. If the AI goes wrong, the mistake is in the house plan, not in the construction.

The Workflow with SDD [00:49]: We explain the 4 steps of the approach (as exemplified by the GitHub Spec Kit): Specify, Plan, Break in Tasks and Implement.

The Change in Developer Role [01:40]: The future is less about writing code and more about designing systems and clearly defining the intention of the product.

SDD does not replace TDD or BDD; it acts in a top layer, defining the intention of the product to guide Artificial Intelligence in generating consistent codes.

Watch and find out if the future of software development is in code or specify clearly!
